note: Maps which underlying capabilities matter in which domain, and proposes evaluation tailored to the domain rather than to a general benchmark.
title: Fundamental Capabilities and Applications of Large Language Models: A Survey
explain_beginner: Large language models work well in many fields, but we don't fully understand which of their core strengths matter most for different jobs. This survey maps out the fundamental abilities these models possess and shows how different domains rely on different combinations of these abilities. Rather than using one-size-fits-all tests, the researchers suggest evaluating models based on the specific skills each field actually needs, making it easier to choose the right model for the job.
explain_business: When deploying language models in production, selecting the right model requires understanding which capabilities matter for your specific application. This research provides a practical framework to identify which model strengths align with your domain's actual needs, whether healthcare, legal services, or financial analysis. Rather than relying on generic performance scores, companies can now evaluate models against the precise capabilities their business processes require, reducing deployment risk and improving real-world outcomes.
explain_practitioner: This survey systematically documents LLM fundamental capabilities, their formation mechanisms, and interconnections, then analyzes their application across nine domains including medicine, law, finance, and software engineering. The authors establish explicit mappings between specific capabilities and domain-specific requirements, revealing that standard benchmarks often misalign with real-world performance needs. The key contribution is domain-tailored evaluation frameworks that prioritize assessing capabilities relevant to each application's unique demands rather than universal performance metrics.
